en: A fine, dotted dress. Pretty airy in the area of the chest.
A large cloak. It ensures that the upper body of its wearer stays hidden. ^orange;(Hides the wearer's body)
A hood with an unusual design. Comfy nonetheless.
Surprisingly light for an obelisk. Not as surprisingly light for a MYSTERIOUS obelisk.
Mysterious for sure, but they seem impractical for running. ^orange;(Hides the wearer's body)
Surprisingly light for an obelisk. Not as surprisingly light for a MYSTERIOUS obelisk.
Whoever dons this hood is sure to conceal their identity.
With a ruff this big, you're never going to soil your clothes while eating!
Robes tailored after those of the second Grand Protector.
Designed after one of humanity's most famous paintings.
Participating in a fight with only some sort of bathrobe on seems like a silly idea.
Does this skirt protect you effectively? No. Does it feel comfy under this skirt? Absolutely.
It's hard to tell from scarce depictions, if the Cultivator wears a helmet, or posesses a helmet-like head.
A sturdy belt, that doesn't cover much of the lower body.
Most renditions of the Cultivator depict arm bands and a few plates on the chest.
It IS a rather curious apple, that stays in front of your face.
There is something particularly curious about this bowl hat. Seems like it's missing something...
An apple-bowl-hat-combo. Quite a curious sense of fashion.
This suit is curiously simple. The tie is as red as a sweet apple.
This kind of helmet used to be worn by some old earthen police forces. The Peacekeepers partially revived the active use of it.
A surprisingly light bundle of coverings for your lower body.
A pretty armet. Not that practical, but pretty.
It isn't nearly as protective as it is shiny.
These tassets sure couldn't deflect an arrow, but you can almost see your reflection on them!
Makes you almost feel as famous as the artist, who had clothes similar to these.
Designed after the headwear, which is shown in the self-portrait of a revered artist.
A wooden cane, meant for transporting a small selection of wares.
A light and striped cloak. Perfect for a peddling Frogg merchant.
It's unusual for Froggs to wear pants this long. Probably easier on the eyes for the merchant's customers.
A light coat usually worn by the swamp-inhabiting Frogg.
A light coat, usually worn by the swamp-inhabiting Frogg. ^orange;(Goes into the leg slot)
This jacket doesn't seem all that big, for someone named Big Ape.
The buckles on the shoes are gloriously oversized and useless.
A colonial print apron. Its design dates way back in human history.
The suit jacket covers a firm overall and a shirt.
Awfully simple, for a grand cloak.
This grand skirt only reaches as far as your knees. Not that grand, sure, but pretty breezy.
There isn't much of a difference between this uniform and the one before it. Except the gloves.
The first of the Grand Protector's robes, to feature the later commonplace shoulder pads.
The most recent rendition of the Grand Protector's outfit. The destruction of Earth made it the last of its kind.
This helmet's design slightly differs from depictions of the Cultivator, by leaving the back of the wearer's head exposed.
A very ornate garment. Seems almost too ornate, to only be used for doing poetic stuff.
Sometimes also refered to as millstone collar. Just a fancier way to not soil your clothes while dining.
A more casual, and comfier, variant of the Protectorate's usual uniform.
Commonly worn by Protectors, who weren't out in the field.
The design of these robes is inspired by those, which were worn by the very first Grand Protector.
The light top of a dress, which comes with a dark pearl necklace. A few weasel hairs seem to be stuck to it...
A simple thin headband. Pretty quiet, for a headband.
This was the last robe, that came with a long golden band.
The last of the Grand Protector's outfits to be adorned with ornate accessoires.
A much subtler headscarf than the other version. The earring though, remains as subtle as before.
This exotic dress isn't as subtle as the usual dress, but pretty subtle for an exotic one.
Well, the headscarf itself isn't that subtle, but the small pearl earring is!
You could swear, that the coat is giving off an unusual, but comforting warmth.
This strange hat gives you the feeling, that someone out there appreciates what you've done.
These pants somehow give your legs the will to wander further on!
Could be anything. It's supposed to be an Apex though. Trust me.
This mask somehow looks scarier than an actual Floran. Probably because it doesn't look like an actual Floran.
This mask is supposed to look like a Glitch... Not even close.
This mask is supposed to be a warning specifically for the Grounded. Could probably offend all of Avian-kind.
Looks like a really hungry birdman.
Yes, this used to be part of the game. I despise its existence wholeheartedly.
This outfit and its successors, resembled uniforms more than robes.
This robe's design was the first to greatly differ from its predecessors.
A fine tailoring shop run by Katyusha Smirnoff and her trusty companion, Leonid.
ko: 카츄샤 스미르노프와 그녀의 믿음직한 동료 레오니드가 운영하는 훌륭한 재봉점입니다.

en: Expertly, hand-made garments for a considerable price!
